A faithful refutation of the canonical conjunction. printedSigma uses conditional covariances given the entire sample design, including the diagonal and all ordered distinct overlapping pairs, exactly as equation (2). trueTarget uses the actual unconditional score variance as equation (1). The weak-limit conjunct asserts a mean-zero finite-second-moment law and the specified limiting covariance without adding a Gaussian requirement. Although the universal assertion being negated has the stronger SampleRank premise, an admissible counterexample satisfies it: iid uniform[-1,1] units, X=(1,u+v), Y=(u+v)^2, Q=diag(1,2/3), beta=(2/3,0). Sample rank holds almost surely for every N>=3. Conditional residual covariances vanish because each residual is a function of the observed design, but the intercept score-sum variance at N=3 is 12/5. All quantities are measurable and finite; even fitted residuals are uniformly bounded. Thus the canonical assertion itself fails, not an alternative reading. The witness conditions and rank argument are written in refutation-checks.md; scratch/Checks.lean independently establishes joint satisfiability of every Lean premise.
